description: Use for "how does X work", code walkthroughs before changing something, and placement / ownership / layering questions ("where should this live", "which package owns this", "is this the right layer"). Explains subsystem architecture, runtime flow, onboarding mental models. Use why for motivation.

compare.without: Lists files and functions without showing how the whole fits together.
compare.with: Writes an architectural explanation a senior engineer new to the area could start working from.

compare.without: Edits code while it looks around.
compare.with: Sends one read-only helper, so your code stays untouched.

compare.without: Silently guesses what an unclear question means.
compare.with: States its reading of the question, then explores. You can redirect anytime.

brief.intro: It answers "how does X work" questions. If the scope is unclear, it states its reading and explores, and you can redirect.
sections: Sends one read-only helper that explores and writes the explanation in one pass, aimed at a senior engineer new to the area.
Hands you the helper's text with only light edits for clarity, never a rewrite.

lessons.quote: They should understand the architecture well enough to start working in it confidently.
lessons.quoteTr: They should understand the architecture well enough to start working in it confidently.
lessons.title: Set depth by what the reader can do
lessons.does: It explains until you could start changing this code with confidence, no shallower and no line-by-line tour.
lessons.why: "More detail" has no measure; naming what the reader should be able to do gives the AI a ruler for enough.
lessons.try: Say what you need to do afterward: "Explain enough that I can change this config myself."

lessons.title: Say how much a handoff may change
lessons.does: The main chat passes the helper's explanation to you nearly as written, with light edits for clarity.
lessons.why: Allowing light edits and ruling out a rewrite stops the AI from squeezing a good explanation into its own lossy summary.
lessons.try: When the AI tidies someone else's text: "Fix typos and breaks, add a line of context if needed, but don't rewrite it."

lessons.quote: If the scope is ambiguous, state your interpretation and explore.
lessons.quoteTr: If the scope is ambiguous, state your interpretation and explore.
lessons.title: State your reading, then start
lessons.does: When the question is vague, it says how it reads it and gets going; you can redirect any time.
lessons.why: Saying its reading out loud means it doesn't stall waiting for you, and you can see if it misread.
lessons.try: Add: "Where I'm unclear, write one line on how you read it, then keep going without waiting for me."

blocks: Explore the codebase to answer "how does X work?" questions.
If the scope is ambiguous, state your interpretation and explore. The user can redirect.

Spawn one read-only general-purpose subagent that explores and explains in one pass: `Task` with `subagent_type: generalPurpose` and `readonly: true` in Cursor, `Agent` in Claude Code (`subagent_type: general-purpose`), `task` in OpenCode (`subagent_type: general`), `spawn_agent` in Codex. If your harness has no subagent tool, as in Pi without an extension, do the exploring and writing yourself. Give it the user's question and this brief:

> You are writing an architectural explanation for a senior engineer. Explore the codebase and write an explanation that a senior engineer unfamiliar with this area could read and walk away with a solid mental model. They should understand the architecture well enough to start working in it confidently. You have read-only access to the codebase.
Present the subagent's output. Light edits for clarity or context from the conversation are fine. Do not substantially rewrite it.
